findings.reason: citing the resolver to call turns a new resolution implementation into a call to one owner, which is the whole point of the section.
findings.text: §60 says store_review "validates neither sha" and adds resolution, but names no existing resolver to reuse; the codebase already answers "does this revision name a commit" in reports._commit_resolves_in, promotion._commit_canonical_id and recovery._resolve_commit, and asks it a fifth time rather than reusing one of them

findings.reason: the section should name recovery._review_head_and_tree as the owner of the reviewed head and reports._commit_resolves_in as the resolver, or it ships a second and third copy of the same question.
findings.text: §60 also promises the refusal "names the reviewed worktree's actual head", which is the job of recovery._review_head_and_tree / _reviewed_run_head (reckon/crew/recovery.py:357, :1528); a sha-resolution check written into store_review beside those owners forks review-head resolution a third time

findings.reason: the owner to extend is reckon/service.py (promote the XDG-aware directory resolver there and let systemd_user_dir delegate), otherwise the plan as written introduces a crew<->service dependency cycle.
findings.text: §61's done-when says "every unit path resolves through systemd_user_dir()" (reckon/crew/paid_lanes.py:750), but the unit-path/installed/write_unit/systemctl/linger facility it is consolidating lives in reckon/service.py, and paid_lanes already imports reckon.service (reckon/crew/paid_lanes.py:841, :906); routing service.unit_path through a crew module inverts that dependency

findings.reason: the section already names the owner and the reuse target, so the finding is that the plan is correct here, not that it needs to change.
findings.text: SystemdUserWatchService already delegates active/lingering/enable_linger/start to reckon.service but keeps its own unit_path (hardcoding ~/.config/systemd/user) and a verbatim copy of service.write_unit's unchanged-content check; §61 identifies this correctly, so this line records that the plan's own citation is accurate and the fix named (extend reckon/service.py, parameterised by unit name) is the right remedy

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no implementable section adds a module; §60 and §21 extend existing functions (store_review, promotion's shortfall report) and §61 removes a module rather than adding one, so no new surface is spread over shared machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §60 adds a fifth commit-resolution site instead of extending an owner, and §61 names systemd_user_dir() (a crew module) as the resolver owner when the generic facility lives in reckon/service.py.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §60 proposes a new commit-resolution check in store_review (reckon/crew/review.py:1339) without citing the four resolvers that already exist for exactly this question (reckon/crew/reports.py:1494 _commit_resolves_in, reckon/crew/promotion.py:443 _commit_canonical_id, reckon/crew/recovery.py:378 _resolve_commit and :1461 _resolve_abbreviated_commit).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §61 explicitly justifies routing the watcher's render/write/control through reckon/service.py rather than forking it, and the retained SystemdUserWatchService is the documented injectable fake-manager seam (reckon/crew/runs.py:3424), so the plan extends an owner instead of forwarding to one.
